_about.authoredOrGenerated: AUTHORED. The only editable source for a component's public shape. Vue/SCSS and the Figma library are generated VIEWS of it; neither may update the other directly (contract-first).
_about.whyNotInContractsDir: This example lives in docs/examples/ because scripts/build-catalog.mjs and scripts/check-contracts.mjs enumerate every contracts/*.json — a file placed there is treated as a real contract.

audiences.consumer agent: an agent USING the system to build pages/designs. Enters via catalog/catalog.json (or, on claude.ai, via the injected claude-design/readme.md and never sees contracts at all). Reads a contract's STRUCTURAL fields — options, values, defaults, slots — to learn what legitimately exists.
audiences.builder agent: an agent CHANGING the system (tokens, contracts, Figma, the generated views). Reads contracts in full at the moment of modification; the HISTORY fields (changes[], knownIssues[]) exist for this audience, to stop decided questions from being re-litigated.
audiences.checkers: deterministic scripts (no model). Read only the structural fields listed per-field below.
audiences.human: maintainers and designers reviewing PRs or tracing a decision.

_about.validatedBy: scripts/check-contracts.mjs against contracts/contract.schema.json (shape, options vs real Vue props, tokensUsed resolution, one-contract-claims-each-token)
moreInfo: contracts/README.md — the full story: why contracts exist, the contract-first workflow, what belongs in a contract (the contract-fact / ruling / build-narrative table), the migration pipeline
https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/ — the schema dialect the checker's walker implements a deliberate subset of

name.purpose: Stable component id (kebab-case). The join key across every artifact.
consumedBy: check-contracts.mjs (composedOf targets must name a real contract)
name.notConsumedBy: check-figma.mjs — it keys its contract map by FILE PATH (check-figma.mjs:316) and joins to Figma via identity.figma.componentSetName. It never reads this field.

version.purpose: Semver for the PUBLIC SHAPE. Moves when rendered output or the option surface changes; deliberately does NOT move for a declined proposal (see changes[]).
consumedBy: build-catalog.mjs (copied into catalog.json — so a version edit requires regenerating catalog/)

description.purpose: One-line summary of what the component is.
description.audience: consumer agents (it is copied into catalog.json, their entry point)

identity.purpose: Where each view of this component lives. Traceability, not behavior.
identity.kind: component (default; codePath is a .vue file, options diffed against real props) | foundation (shared behavior, codePath is an SCSS partial) | pattern (a prescribed COMPOSITION — no codePath, names its parts in composedOf). The enum IS in contract.schema.json:35-42 and the walker enforces it (check-contracts.mjs:46-49). What lives in the CHECKER rather than the schema is the conditional that a component/foundation must have a codePath while a pattern must not (check-contracts.mjs:83-85) — JSON Schema cannot express that dependency cleanly.
identity.codePath_scssPath_relatedPaths_downstrea: Repo paths (and downstream SiteNow mirrors). codePath is machine-read (check-contracts diffs options against the Vue file; build-catalog copies it); the rest are human/builder traceability prose.
identity.registeredName_storybookId: The component's name in the barrel export / Storybook. storybookId is copied into catalog.json.

figma.fileKey_componentSetName_componentSetId_: Anchors into the Figma library. componentSetName and the set's variant axes are verified against the committed figma/snapshot.json by check-figma.mjs. componentSetName is part of check-figma's staleness hash — renaming it demands a Figma sync + snapshot re-stamp.
figma.note: What the set IS (axes, values, variant count). maxLength 600 in contract.schema.json:98 — the ONLY maxLength anywhere in the schema. Note it is enforced as a WARNING (check-contracts.mjs:54-59 pushes to warnings, and the script exits on errors only), so an over-cap note does not fail check:drift. It once grew to 3,292 chars doing five jobs; the four fields below are those jobs' proper homes.
figma.axisRationale: WHY the axes are shaped this way — the part a later builder agent must not re-litigate (the stock example is Button collapsing a naive boolean explosion down to a small axis set; do not quote a specific pair of numbers here, since the live set's variantCount moves — read figma/snapshot.json). Prose; no script reads it.
figma.measured: Values measured off the BUILT set, so a verification pass compares against what was actually drawn. Prose; no script reads it.
figma.deliberateOmissions: What the set does NOT draw and why — so nobody 'completes' it and reintroduces the problem the omission avoided. Prose; no script reads it.
figma.precedent: The earlier component whose pattern this follows. Prose; no script reads it.

identity.claudeDesign: Anchor into the Claude Design view (project id / template name). Prose pointer; no script reads it.

options.purpose: THE PUBLIC API. Each option maps one concept to BOTH a code prop and a Figma axis/property — the triple mapping is the whole point of the contract.
options.audience: consumer agents (what may I use?), builder agents (what must both views implement?), checkers (does reality match?)

perOptionFields.name: Machine-read by all five scripts. Part of check-figma's staleness hash.
perOptionFields.type: enum | string | boolean | ... Checked against the real Vue prop type by check-contracts.mjs. check-claude-design.mjs does NOT check type — it compares the template's enum VALUES (as a subset) and its DEFAULTS, both as warnings, and reads opt.type only to decide whether a default comparison is meaningful.
perOptionFields.values: The complete legal enum values — the authority behind rule components-from-catalog. check-claude-design.mjs warns when a .dc.html template's own enum is not a subset of this list; nothing here checks a generated PAGE against it.
perOptionFields.default: Checked against the Vue prop default (check-contracts) and the template default (check-claude-design).
perOptionFields.status: active | planned | deprecated (schema enum, contract.schema.json:166-172; contracts/logo.json:109 uses active). Rule no-planned-options tells consumer agents not to use planned ones; no checker in this repo enforces it, so this field is guidance the agent must honour.
perOptionFields.description: Prose for agents/humans. No script reads it.
perOptionFields.code.prop: The Vue prop name check-contracts.mjs diffs against. code.notes / code.class are prose.
perOptionFields.figma.axis + figma.map: The Figma variant axis and the option-value -> variant-label mapping. Verified against the snapshot by check-figma.mjs; BOTH are in the staleness hash — editing either demands a Figma sync. figma.property / figma.notes are prose.

slots.purpose: Content areas, INCLUDING behavioral side effects of slot presence (e.g. Brand Bar's second_row_content silently forcing narrow styling — visible in neither tool).
slots.consumedBy: No checker in this repo. check-claude-design.mjs deliberately skips slots when it compares a template's props to the contract — .dc.html has no slot mechanism, so slot content is templated as ordinary editor props. Slots are read by agents and humans only.

tokensUsed.purpose: The tier-3 tokens this component consumes. Names match Figma variables 1:1. INVARIANT: every component-tier token is claimed by exactly ONE contract.
tokensUsed.audience: checkers primarily; consumer agents follow the names into catalog/tokens.lean.json for resolved values
consumedBy: check-figma.mjs (bound variables on the Figma set must be a subset of this list)
tokensUsed.warning: Part of check-figma's staleness hash — adding/removing an entry demands a Figma sync + snapshot re-stamp.

behavior.purpose: Verifiable claims about how the component behaves, with file:line citations — rules that live cleanly in neither code comments nor Figma.
consumedBy: nothing — prose, and NOT length-capped. CORRECTED 2026-08-22: an earlier draft of this file said behavior/changes/knownIssues/geometryNotTokenized are 'capped per item by the schema'. They are not. contract.schema.json contains exactly ONE maxLength — line 98, identity.figma.note, 600 — and these items are bare {"type":"string"}. Keeping them short is a discipline, not a guardrail; do not assume a checker will stop you.

changes.purpose: DELIBERATE public-shape decisions: rulings (who, when, what), including DECLINED proposals. Exists so a later builder agent cannot mistake a decision for an oversight and 'fix' it back — e.g. badge's one-fixed-size ruling. A ruling is 1-2 sentences; the blow-by-blow narrative belongs in .claude/sessions/, never here.
changes.audience: builder agents and humans ONLY. A consumer agent never needs this field.
consumedBy: nothing — prose, and NOT length-capped by the schema (see behavior.consumedBy).

knownIssues.purpose: As-shipped bugs, dead code, downstream divergence — recorded instead of silently fixed (the tokenize-as-shipped rule). Honesty that stops agents 'correcting' intentional absences.
consumedBy: nothing — prose, and NOT length-capped by the schema (see behavior.consumedBy).

geometryNotTokenized.purpose: Raw values DELIBERATELY left un-tokenized, each with its argument — so the absence of a token reads as a decision, not a gap.
consumedBy: nothing — prose, and NOT length-capped: additionalProperties is a bare {"type":"string"} (see behavior.consumedBy).

a11y_breakpoints_assets.purpose: Semantics (landmark/attrs), responsive switching notes, asset inventory — facts that live cleanly in neither view.
consumedBy: nothing — prose today. (An audit noted a11y is free-text where a structured, checkable form — element/role/contrast — would be stronger; unadopted.)

children.purpose: Nested component contracts: which contract governs a child, fixed props, inherited props.
consumedBy: check-figma.mjs (children[].contract — in the staleness hash; it widens the allowed bound-token set at check-figma.mjs:362-363)
children.notConsumedBy: check-contracts.mjs does NOT verify the child contract exists — it validates composedOf ids only (lines 86-88). check-figma.mjs:363 does contracts.get(child.contract)?.tokensUsed ?? [], so a bad path silently widens nothing instead of erroring.

composedOf.purpose: For kind: pattern — the real contract ids this pattern arranges. A pattern PINS the options it depends on rather than re-declaring them.
consumedBy: check-contracts.mjs (every id must be a real contract)

_snapshotHashWarning: check-figma.mjs's staleness hash covers ONLY: options[].name, options[].figma.axis, options[].figma.map, tokensUsed, children[].contract, identity.figma.componentSetName (plus token values/aliases). Editing any of these forces a Figma sync + snapshot re-stamp before check:drift can pass. Editing anything ELSE in a contract (all prose/history fields, descriptions, version) never touches Figma — check-figma passing WITHOUT --stamp is the proof.

example.name: badge
example.description: UIDS badge component contract (trimmed illustration — see contracts/badge.json for the real file).

figma.note: 6 variants on one axis: Type (Primary, Secondary, Cool Gray, Blue, Green, Orange).
axisRationale: No Size axis: a size modifier was DECLINED 2026-08-21 (changes[]) — Type is the complete axis list, not a first instalment.

options.name: type
options.description: Colorway. Drives one BEM modifier class.

behavior: Only badge--primary overrides text color, to black (badge.scss:17); the other five modifiers declare only background and inherit the base white.
changes: 2026-08-21 — SIZE MODIFIER DECLINED (the design system owner): one fixed size is the finished answer. Recorded so the absence reads as deliberate; reopening needs a fresh ruling and is contract-first.
knownIssues: type='orange' maps to the {color.status.danger} primitive, not a literal orange hue — stated so it doesn't read as a naming error.

geometryNotTokenized.border: 1px solid transparent (badge.scss:11) — reserves 1px of box size, never paints; per the Border foundation's convention.
